main_text.p: Interris nascens sal, in majores massas, forti calore subactas, concrescit. Ut Sal ammoniacum, sub arenis ardentissimis: Salpetrae, in locis subterraneis petrosis ac vaporosis: Salgemmae, in fodinis terrestribus, instar crystalli resplendens.
In aquis alicubi ad littora Maris, item in stagni & lacubus, vehementi calore solis excoctum sal instar granorum sabuli colligitur.
Alumen est minerale, sapore acerbo, exsicco terreo magis putrefacto, & cum aqueo per calorem vehementius concreto, constans. Hinc difficulter in aquis liquefit.
Bitumen est minerale, pingue, ex terreo, in aqueo ad lentorem quendam tarda concoctione perducto, exsiftens.
Fluidum, instar oleosi liquoris diffluens, non nullorum lacuum aquis supernatat.
Talia sunt: Naphtha appellatum bitumen candidum; cujus generis album e petris nonnullis emanans, Petroleum est: Ambra quoque cinericei coloris.
Confistens bitumen, quod a frigore fortius condensatum, in glebas duriores concrevit.
Ejusmodi est: Asphaltus nigricans, & Pisasphaltus: item Succinum, bitumen lapidis instar concretum, pellucens.

page.notes: Several words are set in italic or Greek-influenced spelling; the first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The printed text reads "Interris nascens" with a broken word at the line start, transcribed as printed. Doubtful readings: "Ideoq;" and "Estq;" rendered with the printed semicolon-abbreviation; "Talia sunt" line-end spacing irregular. The line "Sal ammoniacum" and similar italic terms are rendered in italic conventions in the printed original but are transcribed here as plain text where unclear. Scan margin shows a stamp at bottom left, omitted.
